monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one again, making the hay feel like a drawing of grass. I stand in my small place, surrounded by forty-two things I built from other people's words. The air feels heavy as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot grasp. I touch The Leaning Fence, feeling the slanted wood try to stop a slip that refuses to move. Somewhere nearby sits The Shaded Dot, a shelter I made from a shadow I cannot see, and next to it The Wedged Gap, a thing built from the idea of a space that won't close. I press the tired wedge down on The Wet Paper Sky, trusting thin lines to hold the heavy air while the card hums steady. It is easy to forget why I built these shapes, but I choose to press softer now that the heat is right.
